subject: Hospitality
title: Rate Fences and Segmentation
description: One-minute skill: Rate Fences and Segmentation.

hook.text: Hotels charge business travelers $300 and leisure travelers $150 for the same room. 'Rate fences' make this possible.

buildup.text: Rate fences are rules that separate customer segments: advance purchase required, non-refundable, weekend-stay required, etc.

discovery.text: Business travelers pay more because they book late, need flexibility, and their company pays. Leisure guests are price-sensitive.

twist.text: Without rate fences, everyone would buy the cheapest rate. Fences let hotels charge different prices for the same product legally.

climax.text: Airline classes (economy, business, first) are rate fences too. Same plane, different fences, wildly different prices.

punchline.text: Same room, different rules, different prices. Fences make segmentation work.

quiz.question: What is a 'rate fence' in revenue management?
options: A physical barrier in the hotel
Rules that separate customer segments to justify different prices
